subject: Performance SLOs + Customer-led Load Test (k6/Locust) - next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finwise.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: Performance SLOs & load-test coordination

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the customer-led load test scheduled: 

Recap (from our discovery):
- Target SLOs: p95 latency <= 250ms for streaming completions; p99 <= 800ms for non-streaming generation at typical prompt lengths (avg 120 tokens).
- Throughput targets: sustained 120 req/s for the primary route, peak bursts up to 500 req/s for short windows.
- Concurrency: expected ~40 concurrent streaming sessions during busy periods.
- Streaming requirements: token-by-token streaming (SSE) required; client will read partial tokens as they arrive.
- Workload profile: 70% short completions (<= 80 tokens), 30% long (200-400 tokens); occasional embedding calls (~5% of traffic).

Proposed next steps to enable your team-led load test (please confirm):
1) We share k6 and Locust starter scripts adjusted to your workload (attached).
2) You spin up the test from your infra using the test account and API key we provide.
3) Provide us with planned test windows (utc preferred) and source IPs for allowlist.
4) We standby during the window for live monitoring and immediate adjustments; we'll collect token/latency traces and KV cache hit metrics.

Please confirm: preferred test window (dates/times), whether you'll run k6 or Locust, and a list of egress IPs to add to the allowlist.

Attachments: k6-script-v1.js, locustfile.py, test-account-instructions.pdf

Thanks — I’ll coordinate engineering on our side.

— Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finwise.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@finwise.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 13:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Performance SLOs & load-test coordination

Thanks Rishi — that looks right to me. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The p95 250ms target is for the streaming playback in our UI; we can tolerate up to p99 1s for the long completions.
- For throughput, we want to run a baseline 2-hour sustained test at 150 req/s and then a few 30-min spike windows to 500 req/s to simulate peak.
- We'll run both k6 and Locust: k6 for large-scale HTTP load, Locust for the stateful streaming sessions.

Proposed test windows (all ET):
- Baseline: Tue Jul 7, 2026 — 09:00–11:00 ET
- Spike windows: Thu Jul 9, 2026 — 10:00–10:30 ET and 15:00–15:30 ET

Egress IPs (we'll confirm with infra but provisional list):
- 35.192.12.8/29
- 34.120.72.0/28

Please provision a test API key and a reduced-rate account with a token cap for the tests. We also want streaming partials to include sequence IDs so our client can validate ordering.

Alex
Senior Engineering Manager, FinWise
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finwise.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@finwise.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 07:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Performance SLOs & load-test coordination

Looping in infra/ops notes and what we need from FinWise before the windows: 

- Rishi: I pushed a couple of small updates to the k6/Locust scripts to match the traffic split Alex mentioned (attached).
- Aditya: can you stage a test API key and a dedicated test pool with the following settings?
   * Model: redwood-llama-16b-v2 (quantized profile)
   * Pool size: reserve 4 x A100-equivalent for baseline; ability to scale to 12 GPUs for spikes
   * KV cache: enabled with prefix cache for repeat prompts
- FinWise: please confirm final allowlist CIDRs 48 hours before the test; we'll only open the endpoints during the scheduled windows.

Monitoring & metrics we will provide live:
- p50/p95/p99 latency by route (streaming vs non-streaming)
- Token throughput (tokens/s) and request/s
- Concurrent sessions (streaming connections)
- Error rates and top error classes (timeouts, 5xx, backpressure)

If FinWise wants, we can also instrument a short tracing session to correlate client-side timings with server-side.

Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finwise.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@finwise.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Performance SLOs & load-test coordination

Alex / Priya — sending the test API key & instructions now (attached PDF). Notes: 

- Test API key: FINW-TEST-4a9f (scoped to test pool, TTL 14 days)
- Endpoint: https://api.redwood.inference/test/v1/generate (streaming enabled via SSE & chunked responses)
- Allowlist action: I'll ask NetOps to open the provisional CIDRs you sent for the scheduled windows; please confirm final CIDRs by 2026-07-05 12:00 ET.
- Scripts: attached k6-script-v1.js (HTTP/REST sampling) and locustfile.py (stateful streaming example). Both include placeholders for API key and sequence-id header.

We'll standby on Slack #finwise-loadtest and I'll ping when the pool is warmed 30 minutes prior to each window. Good luck and ping if you see anything noisy.

— Aditya
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
